title: Exceptional surface states v1
description: The eight states every surface has to render besides the one where everything worked, and what each one is derived from. docs/product/PRODUCT_SPEC.md and the owning state machines are the normative owners. Each exceptional state either names a registered machine and the states of it that produce it, or declares that it is client-local and derived from nothing on the server — and the validator resolves the first kind against packages/schemas/state-machine-registry-v1.json, so a state cannot be rendered from a lifecycle that does not exist. Two rules run through all of them: a surface never invents a policy the server did not send, and an exceptional state never discloses more than the ordinary one it replaced.

origin.description: client-local states are derived from the client's own situation — a request in flight, a cache older than its freshness budget — and from nothing the server sends. server-derived states name the machine and the states of it that produce them.

authorization_input.description: An input_id in packages/schemas/projection-authorization-v1.json, for a state produced by an authorization decision rather than by a lifecycle.

disclosure.description: What the state is allowed to tell the person looking at it. indistinguishable-from-absent is the strongest: the surface must not let a viewer tell this state from the subject simply not existing, which is what stops a private profile and a blocked one from being distinguishable.

recovery_action.description: What the person can do. none is a real answer and is recorded rather than left as an empty affordance.
